paragraphs: Ilfa told Rabbah bar bar Chana, “You, Rabbi Yochanan’s students, act like him; we will act like Rabbi Chanina,” Bammeh Ishah 60b. But the Gemara reads Ifa; Rashi: Ifa son of Rachava (see there). This reading is difficult: Rachava, Ifa’s father, was Rav Yehudah’s student (see there), while Rabbah bar bar Chana was Rabbi Yochanan’s student and Ilfa his colleague. Though Rabbah bar bar Chana was also in Rav Yehudah’s time (see there), it seems unlikely to me that he was in Ifa son of Rachava’s time, Rachava being Rav Yehudah’s student. There is another reason to read Ilfa speaking to Rabbah bar bar Chana: both were in the Land of Israel, whereas Ifa and Avimi were Pumbedita’s sharp scholars. Their father Rachava was also from there, and they studied Shevuot at Rabbah’s academy; he was head in Pumbedita. Apparently the Rabbah bar bar Chana in Rav Yehudah’s time, whom Rav Yehudah visited when ill, was the second Rabbah bar bar Chana, Rabbi’s student. When he descended to Babylonia, Rabbi authorized him to judge and permit firstborn animals (see there). But Rabbah bar bar Chana, Rabbi Yochanan’s student, was not in Babylonia. Rav Yehudah too was head in Pumbedita, so Rachava was his student. Rashi, end of Metzi'at Ha'ishah: Ilfa, a sage, Rabbi Yochanan’s colleague. They were poor and went into commerce. Rabbi Yochanan heard an angel intending to punish them for abandoning Torah; another angel said to his fellow that one of them was destined for greatness. Ilfa did not hear. Rabbi Yochanan said, “Conclude that the time is mine,” returned, was appointed, and became wealthy. Ilfa hung from a ship’s mast and said, “Whoever asks me from Rabbi Oshaya’s baraita, and I cannot resolve it from the Mishnah—I shall fall and drown.” An elder asked him, “One who says, Give a shekel to my sons,” etc., Ta'anit 21a. Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin, chapter 1, halakhah 1: Chalfi said, “Seat me on the riverbank. If I do not derive Rabbi Chiyya the great’s baraita from the Mishnah, throw me in the river.” (See Chalfai: in Jerusalem-Talmud usage this is Ilfa.) Rabbi Yehudah bar Chiyya made a statement. Ilfa heard it and reported it before Rav Padda, Zevachim 13b. Rabbi Yochanan said, “Ilfa asks,” Zevachim 20, beginning of a. Rabbi Yochanan spoke in his name in the new editions, and there 21a. Rabbi Yirmeyah in his name. Chalfi asked, “Can gleanings become consecrated as they fall?”, Pe'ah, at ס״ז [locator unresolved]. Sedeh Yehoshua writes this is Ilfa of the Babylonian Talmud: Temurah 25a, Ilfa asked concerning gleanings as they fall.
